title: Binary Search
definition: Binary Search works on sorted data and repeatedly checks the middle value.
realLifeExample: Looking up a word in a dictionary by opening near the middle is binary search.

algorithm.Iterative:
(Binary Search) BINARY(DATA, LB, UB, ITEM, LOC)

1. Set BEG := LB, END := UB and MID := INT((BEG + END) / 2).
2. Repeat while BEG <= END and DATA[MID] != ITEM.
3. If ITEM < DATA[MID], set END := MID - 1; else set BEG := MID + 1.
4. Set MID := INT((BEG + END) / 2).
5. If DATA[MID] = ITEM, set LOC := MID; else set LOC := NULL.
6. Exit.
algorithm.Functions:
FUNCTION BINARY(DATA, LB, UB, ITEM)

1. Set BEG := LB, END := UB.
2. Repeat while BEG <= END:
   Set MID := INT((BEG + END) / 2).
   If DATA[MID] = ITEM, return MID.
   If ITEM < DATA[MID], set END := MID - 1; else set BEG := MID + 1.
3. Return NULL.

MAIN:
1. Read DATA, LB, UB, ITEM.
2. LOC := BINARY(DATA, LB, UB, ITEM).
3. Print LOC.
algorithm.Recursion:
FUNCTION BINARY(DATA, BEG, END, ITEM)

1. If BEG > END, return NULL.
2. Set MID := INT((BEG + END) / 2).
3. If DATA[MID] = ITEM, return MID.
4. If ITEM < DATA[MID], return BINARY(DATA, BEG, MID - 1, ITEM).
5. Else return BINARY(DATA, MID + 1, END, ITEM).
